name: DIGITAL COLONY COUNTER
desc: Premium Microprocessor-Based Digital Colony Counter engineered for rapid and high-precision enumeration of bacterial and microorganism colonies. Features a 120 mm clear working plate size integrated with a Wolf Flue gel grid glass plate and a 4-digit resettable LED digital counter.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Digital Colony Counter is a high-precision microprocessor-based enumeration workstation designed for rapid, accurate quantification of bacterial and fungal colonies on standard agar plates. It operates on the principle of uniform transmitted illumination combined with a 100 mm magnifying lens and a Wolf Flue gel grid glass plate, allowing microbiologists, pathologists, and food/water quality analysts to visually distinguish and manually mark colony-forming units (CFUs) with an automated beep confirmation and 4-digit LED tally. In medical pathology, it supports viable plate counts (VPC), total aerobic microbial count (TAMC), and total yeast and mold count (TYMC) per ISO 4833-1, ISO 21527, and USP <61>/<62>; in academic B.Sc/M.Sc laboratories it is used for Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Bacillus subtilis enumeration on nutrient agar, MacConkey agar, and plate count agar; in PhD research and industrial microbiology, it aids in antibiotic susceptibility testing, bioremediation viability assays, and water/wastewater analysis for heterotrophic plate count (HPC) under ISO 6222, including enumeration of microorganisms cultured in the presence of disinfectants or antimicrobial agents.
sop: Ensure the instrument is placed on a clean, level, vibration-free bench away from direct sunlight and corrosive fumes; connect to 230 V AC, 50 Hz single phase mains and switch ON.
Clean the 120 mm Wolf Flue gel grid glass plate and 100 mm diameter magnifying lens with 70% ethanol or isopropanol using lint-free tissue; allow to dry completely.
Place the prepared agar plate (e.g., nutrient agar, MacConkey agar, plate count agar) centrally on the counting zone.
Press the 'SET' button once to enter the target count threshold mode for the batch or maximum expected CFU count.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., 0 to reset baseline or 9999 count limit) as per the laboratory test protocol.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value.
Press the reset button to ensure the 4-digit LED display reads 0000 before starting a new count.

Remove the petri dish lid and observe colonies through the magnifying lens under uniform cool fluorescent illumination; mark each colony on the glass or petri dish with a felt-tip pen. The counter automatically increments by one and beeps per touch.
Record the final 4-digit LED count after complete scanning; repeat for reproducible triplicate or duplicate plates if required.

Safety Warning: Do not count open agar plates of pathogenic microorganisms (BSL-2 or higher) outside a biological safety cabinet unless proper aseptic containment and decontamination protocols are followed; after use, wipe down with 70% ethanol and dispose of marked plates as biohazardous waste to prevent cross-contamination.
